notes.title: Troubleshooting & How to Fix Softlocking.
notes.content: [h1]Troubleshooting & How to Fix Softlocking[/h1][p][/p][p]Hello![/p][p]Here's a quick post with some troubleshooting that could help you fix some issues you may be having with the game. We will be updating this page if necessary in the future. [/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]i have found a bug/glitch/error, where can I report it so it can get fixed?[/h3][p]Please report any bugs, errors or glitches on our [url="https://discord.gg/9sAJv2Fm98"]Discord Server[/url].[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]I can't get a certain achievement, what is happening?[/h3][p]There's a chance you either aren't connected to Steam, or that the game had some issues connecting to its server. We recommend restarting the game, and checking the small status text below the Main Menu buttons to see if you're connected.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]I am softlocked and cannot continue the level proplery, what should I do?[/h3][p]We recommend resetting the level on the "Chapters" option in the Main menu.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]How to reset your Save File in case of a complete SoftLock / Loading issues with chapter selector:[/h3][p]If, in any case, you cannot continue playing the game because of the game saving a checkpoint with a softlock (this means, that it won't allow you to continue playing properly) or the chapter selector not loading the level properly, do the following:[/p][p][/p][olist][*][p][b]Open the game, and while it's open, go to the following path:[/b][/p][p][/p][p]C:\\Users\\(YOUR WINDOW'S USER NAME)\\AppData\\LocalLow\\Carpincho Studio\\La Salamanca[/p][p][/p][p][i](You can also get there by pressing Windows + R, and pasting "AppData\\LocalLow\\Carpincho Studio\\La Salamanca")[/i][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p][b]Once in that folder, delete ONLY the following files:[/b][/p][p][/p][p]- colliderstate.json[/p][p]- objstate.json[/p][p]- savefile.json[/p][p][/p][p][u]Make sure you only delete those three files and no others while the game is open.[/u][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p][b]Close and reopen the game.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Load the desired level.[/b][/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]I have played a certain level, but it is not available on the chapter selector, what should I do?[/h3][p]In that case, we can provide you a quick fix by giving you a Save File that automatically unlocks all levels. You can contact any of the devs via our [url="https://discord.gg/9sAJv2Fm98"]Discord Server[/url].[/p]

notes.title: DEVBLOG #4 | Map Showcases, Mechanic Overhouls, OST Preview & More!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/7564d543a820dde82727537f44f8eba6a4e4da76.png[/img]

[h3]Hello everyone![/h3]
Welcome to our fourth Devblog here on Steam. It's been some time since the last time we made a DevBlog, so we have quite a lot to show you!

This DevBlog will showcase some parts of the game that have been overhauled and some others that are brand new, such as the Original Soundtrack & a new Enemy that hasn't been revealed yet...

Keep in mind, none of these changes are applied to the Demo, and probably won't be until closer to release.

[h2][u]Chapter Map Showcase[/u][/h2]
During this time, one of our developers has been working on improving some of the older levels of the game so they are at the same quality as the newer ones. At the same time, we wanted to show you an overall look at some of the most creepy and interesting areas of each chapters' map (Except Chapter 2, since that one didn't change much):

[h3][b]Prologue (The Portal):[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/2967f4c12e6bf12ccf7b3a177fff88e8e1af2391.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/9967861e5ddf6aafec7f1735555649651d246cda.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/f1b8b17f7aeff0d84f88fb46f07a3c44ff9e5c6a.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/51eca4dd0179c03f9ee4413dc478b3108e7f5d2f.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Chapter 1 (The Mansion):[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/d6a4a3cacac20342da2e18c38dbaaa41406a038f.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/031bb4eebfc06f0f720b6baf1f6bed6f75aee669.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/85776e3ecb47bec901a1eee48d7456bf7a9c1f23.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/2f01822239de35e917952d38ef6af147401fa871.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Chapter 3 (The Sewers):[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/9c683715641b3d564d85e45a7dcecf14cdb2b8ea.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/a78a43d440c35faa1271e5ab6fc4b3a309d280a2.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/50f1a0f7a288a59e362a3a58c33a7ea629d497d4.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/fbf769c6e7eeb8cb722cdb38d6c4a75d1cd6cc1f.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Chapter 4 (The Tunnels):[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/7a90c5f34f0c5d2a1dbf73e6adeda469ed491d1c.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/8666ef5968edc0f81d92490a6978dbe2f1527501.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/9f802c8eb1f9df91d2a937d1745167b000954d36.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/3da8323b0da08645f20618f2370287436a8a61af.jpg[/img]


[h2][u]Mechanic Overhaul[/u][/h2]
The team here at Carpincho Studio has been working on improving and changing some mechanics that were rather unpolished, unfinished or didn't work that well with players.

[h3][b]Flashlight:[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/46fb3361e489ecee45bd6b38bd1671902d89d002.gif[/img]

Now, [b]the Flashlight has energy that depletes over time[/b]. The flashlight has four states depending the amount of energy it has: [b]High[/b], [b]Medium[/b], [b]Low[/b], and [b]Depleted[/b]. The player will know in which state their flashlight is currently on by looking at the UI that is on the down right corner. At the same time, the light source will change in intensity and range based on the state (Plus, the light will flicker a little bit when transitioning between states). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/cb300d8a4e6d03fdbceca3b04589fe85f19545fe.gif[/img]

To replenish the flashlight's energy, the player will be able to find [b]batteries[/b] around the map:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/85c10520093b2aabf1eec628a81802e2795fd1fd.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Hiding Places:[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/d0ec47ac38ab2becf9e1082ecb8e7338712584fc.gif[/img]

Because of how the code and assets for the old hiding places (like the box or the lockers) worked, to properly implement new ones and to be able to change parts of them if needed, we had to completely overhaul them. The system works pretty much the same, but it should be less buggy and it has better animations!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/14e0e05a32c451632a6b83300279a19ed0805cad.gif[/img]

The most noticeable change is with Lockers, that now work exactly like boxes. Instead of having to open each door of the locker individually, for the sake of consistency, we changed it to a predefined animation that plays instantly when interacting with the locker. 

[i]This also means that The Priest has a new animation for opening lockers![/i]

[h3][b]Items and Inventory:[/b][/h3]
We have slightly changed how interacting with some puzzles work. 

Before, if you interacted with a puzzle and it needed an specific item, if you had that item on your inventory, it would be instantly used and removed from it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/797ac59a3cf9056162a585fdb94773717e1a3298.gif[/img]

Now, instead of instantly removing it, [b]when interacting with a door, a puzzle, or any object that requires an item, the game will automatically open the inventory and the player will have to select the correct item.[/b] In this way, players will be able to have a bit more of choice and interaction with objects in the world.

[h2][u]AI Rework and... New Enemy?[/u][/h2]

In the last months, we have been working on finishing the AI for the main enemies for La Salamanca. 

To be able to easily make new enemies and speed up the whole coding process, we have split parts of the code of our older AI Behaviours on "modules" that can me added to an "agent" (or entity) and be controlled by a Main "script" that runs the entire AI of that specific enemy. This severally speed up the whole process of making new enemies and, right now, we consider that they are pretty much finished.

[b][h3]The Priest[/h3][/b] 
He has remained pretty much the same, but with some optimizations and simplifications on his code, to make sure it works properly. The main change with The Priest is that, now, once he spawns, he won't despawn of the map unless there's a scripted event that requires him to do so.  This means that he will search for the player all around the map all the time, and will use the "Pentagrams" as a method of teleportation to get closer to the player. The Priest will try to always search for the player on the same "area" or section of the map as they are.

[b][h3]The Basilisk [/h3][/b]
It has been completely finished and fully functional. This enemy is similar to The Priest in the sense that it will always wander and search for the player on the same area as they are, but the main difference is that... well, The Basilisk is blind, so they use sound instead as a way find the player.

[i]This means that players will have to be careful and try not to be noisy when close to it, or they may enrage and start chasing them at insane speeds...[/i]

[url=https://www.artstation.com/artwork/3E8lRm](Also, checkout the ArtStation page for it!)[/url]


[b]And lastly, the new and final enemy of La Salamanca: 

[i][h3]The Ghouleh.[/h3][/i][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/918f361fb3d98b6d06a2ace4ed525bb9c658be75.jpg[/img]

This enemy is a bit special, since it doesn't really share that many similarities on behaviour with the other two enemies from the game. Her gameplay and behaviour is quite unique, and the way of attacking the player too.

We would like to reveal more of her, however, we would like to save that surprise for the future. In the mean time, just for you to know... [spoiler]She really hates sunbathing.[/spoiler]

[h2][u]Original Soundtrack Preview[/u][/h2]
During the last months, Carpincho Studio has been actively working with a group of young composers known as "Casa Hornero". 

They have been working on making the OST for La Salamanca! Here's a little preview of what to expect for the final release:

[previewyoutube=K9jctq7AEs4;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3][u]When is this thing releasing?![/u][/h3]
Sadly, we can't give you an exact release date for La Salamanca. However, do know that our plan is to release the game somewhat close to the end of April of this year. So it's not that far away!

[h2]That's all![/h2]
We hope you have enjoyed this Devblog, and that you stay tuned for the coming weeks for news on the game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/e09afe0edbe9ee482b9697a97b086a4c05cc1c47.jpg[/img]
See you in the next DevBlog!

notes.title: La Salamanca's "PARKING" Demo RELEASED!
notes.content:
[h2]Parking Demo Released![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/cf96e6dd2652bec898546387fc1525bd324cedf4.png[/img]

We have recently released the demo for the second chapter of the game, "The Parking". This demo as a focus in stealth and action, with less puzzles. We recommend playing the "Prologue" demo first.

You now will be able to select both the older demo and the new demo in the "Demo Selector" when you click on the "Play" button:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/c1c03d1660295d13999e9ad26eb601346764efc5.png[/img]


[h2]Slow Loading Screens Issue[/h2]

Since this problem still persists, we will mention the existance of this issue again:

We wanted to let you know that we are aware of the issue that some people have with the Demo where the [b]loading screen may take a serious amount of time to load the level (Normally taking around 2 or 5 minutes which is extremely abnormal).[/b] We are investigating the issue and have a potential solution while we try to fix it:

First, it seems that the issue is mainly affected by those who have the game installed on HDD Disks, [b]so we encourage to move the install of the game to a SSD Disk instead if possible.[/b] We will be trying to optimize ther loading of the levels as much as we can so this isn't needed, however we still encourage players to use and SSD Disk since it's overall much more effective than an HDD Disk.

If you find any other issues, please report them on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/mUCVNdEdFb]Discord Server[/url].

In the meantime, we have dropped a small patch with a small warning of loading issue and the Demo Selector that will be fully available on November 8th when we release "The Parking" Demo.

Thank you for your patience and see you soon!

notes.title: DEVBLOG #3 | "The Parking"
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/f0c7a4ceda56729d2a303f4c6dd202292b7e5740.png[/img]

[h3]Hello everyone![/h3]
Welcome to our third Devblog here on Steam, today this Devblog will be split into three parts, the first one dedicated to one of the game's scenarios, "The Parking", the second one about a small sneak peak of the game's enemy AI, and the last one about an event we attended last weekend, Rosario's "Crack Bang Boom".

[h2]What is The Parking?[/h2]
"The Parking Lot" is one of the first levels that was conceived for La Salamanca, a level planned for Chapter II of the story, which had several 'remakes' for some thime before staying on its current final version. It is likely that some images of this level that you have seen before are from outdated versions. The current version is probably the largest and darkest of them all.

Normally, every apartment complex tends to have a parking lot so that residents can store their vehicles in a nearby and safe place, it was clear that a place as large as "El Portal" would have its own. However, this one is considerably larger than many of other complexes, having two full floors, and also functioning as a sort of storage and operations center for some functions of the apartment, such as security and some "employee" needs.

However, this place has been closed for "maintenance" for quite some time, enough for our protagonist to be forced to park his vehicle in front of the entrance of the complex... Why would it take so long? What needs to be fixed in order to be usable again?... it's strange, there are still cars parked, as if they had been abandoned down there...

[h2]Some pictures of The Parking:[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/c6d7609461594ec98403936b1db140aad2dd08f3.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/edff8568126922e1f191c949d48d5722a041b7e1.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/94fde0942acf79a736e1f5821aeb0ccd52d10d59.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/34d209d453e2a1d340aede907bd31804e2dfbdaa.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/2776a31df5baa187e4aeff2cba796900176c6448.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/50f0c7b16aaf54d06fe19c3e0d428c68e4b0358b.jpg[/img]

[h2]Small advancement of enemy AI[/h2]
During all this time, one of our main programmers, Thomás, has been focusing on creating the base for the artificial intelligence of the game's enemies, focusing especially on the AI ​​for "The Priest", one of the most recurring enemies in the game.

[previewyoutube=PPzW4p8rOsg;full][/previewyoutube]
In this little preview, you'll be able to see that the enemy is able to move autonomously around the map, being able to see the player when there are no obstacles in the way, following them and looking for them in the last places they were spotted when they lost sight of them. It is able to open doors and hiding places like lockers, and will kill the player if it is close enough to catch them.

The player is also able to hide behind obstacles, under furniture, or inside certain specific locations on the map, but in this case, The Priest is able to open them if he has seen the player entering one of them.

[b]It should be noted that this is still in an early stage of development, most of the features still need to be polished, and all the animations and models used are temporary, since the new model that we had shown in our second DevBlog is not yet ready to be implemented.[/b]

[h2]¡Tuvimos un Stand en la Crack Bang Boom![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/f4649715249926caa565e2ad0b8196c4fdab901c.png[/img]
Last weekend, the Carpincho Studio team had the opportunity to participate in the international comic convention known as Crack Bang Boom, in Rosario, Santa Fe, Argentina, with a stand dedicated to La Salamanca. At this stand there were three computers so that the public could try out the game's demo and meet the team in person, and we also had limited Carpincho Studio merchandising at the event, in order to fund and recover previous expenses and those of the stand itself.

[previewyoutube=r9wNS7_7KQo;full][/previewyoutube]
[previewyoutube=bdskRzTEr2w;full][/previewyoutube]
We are infinitely grateful to everyone who stopped by the stand and talked to us, tried the demo or supported us with merchandise, if it weren't for people like you, Carpincho Studio and La Salamanca couldn't happen in the same way! And a big thank you to the Crack Bang Boom event for giving us the opportunity to show the game and make something so unique!

[h2]That's all![/h2]
We hope you have enjoyed this Devblog, and that you stay tuned for the coming months, as very interesting and important things are coming for the project.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/b2612ccf6b3356b408066e38f12ff6dfc3ae9c4c.jpg[/img]
See you in the next DevBlog!

notes.title: DEVBLOG #2 | Meet The Priest! (With a brand new 3D Model!)
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/9dc8798c327f4ec1ae180f7b3273eb71a0c82708.png[/img]

[h3]¡Hola a todos![/h3]
Welcome to our second Devblog here on Steam, where we will show the public for the first time the new model for[b] "The Priest"[/b], one of the main enemies of [i]La Salamanca[/i], along with a little information about the character.

[h2]Who's The Priest?[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/b77dd7148169c009694948113a26959dade197e4.png[/img]
The Priest is one of the enemies, if not THE main enemy of "La Salamanca". He falls under the [i]"Stalker" Enemy[/i] category, where there is one particular enemy that always follows the player throughout the game. The Priest will behave this way, searching for the player during almost every level.

If you have played the Demo,[spoiler]this is the enemy that appears multiple times and chases you at the end of the Demo[/spoiler]. In the full game, the Priest will appear at key moments in the story to search for the player throughout the level, and it is during these moments when the player must try not to be spotted by hiding in different places, either behind a pile of boxes, under a table or even inside a closet.

The Priest's origins are... uncertain. Some believe that he was once a very Christian person, who was corrupted by someone or something, probably related to this place. Others, that he is a demon from La Salamanca itself... but, why would he take the form of a Priest then...? In order to know more about who The Priest really is and his history, you will have to investigate on your own in the full game ;).


[h2]Sneak-Peak of the new 3D Model for The Priest[/h2]
The current model found in the game is a free Asset created by [i]Serhat Yucekaya[/i], which despite being of very good quality, this model is only a "placeholder", to be able to show something before that the new design made especially for the game was ready. Today we are going to give you a preview of this new design with its 3D model made by [b][i]Exequiel Devoto[/i][/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/55e19f2b52521ceb6439c8c5c87e2152e21b7151.jpg[/img]
This new model made by shows a much more "Demonic" version of the Priest, with multiple eyes and horns. Inspired by characters like Mr. X or Nemesis from Resident Evil, with Christian elements such as the priest's robe or hanging rosaries (not present in the images shown).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/3543ea39add61f1dda4de40dd3c77b01aba11e95.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/2b2f4c9987c0f7cc00c346459215dc2f81887115.jpg[/img]
It should be noted that the model is not finished, since it is only the base of the model, but we believe that it is more than enough to be able to show it to you and so that you can get a good idea of ​​what is coming. The model is not implemented in the game yet either, this is just a preview, when the model is finished and implemented in the game we will show it on our networks or even [spoiler] in a possible new Demo...[/spoiler]

[b]Finally, we want to thank Exequiel Devoto for giving us the opportunity to work with him, and to be able to bring the Priest to the game as [i]God?[/i] intended![/b]

[h2]That's all![/h2]
We hope you have enjoyed this Devblog, and that you stay tuned for the coming months, as very interesting and important things are coming for the project.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/32876fd92d2f16289f1df23afd4b5c41f7ecd747.png[/img]
See you in the next Devblog!

notes.title: DEVBLOG #1 | ¡The Demo is out on Steam! + The future of the proyect
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/e5999cf6a7e73f416bc528f96a36a441f1d0260a.png[/img]

[h3]¡Hello everyone![/h3]
Welcome to our first Devblog here on Steam, where we will do a short review of some important events related to La Salamanca that happened during this time, and extra information about the future of the project.

[h2]¡The Demo is out on Steam![/h2]
After several months in development, here at Carpincho Studio we prepared a playable Demo of the prologue of [i]“La Salamanca”[/i], and it lasts approximately 20-25 minutes. In this demo, you'll find a VHS tape that one of your friends left for you, seeing everything from his perspective.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/db57ef1937226b0b4545d6ce0bf3d749803c9c99.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/8a5e9b0f4f66a1a99de94662e96d064c36b4a319.jpg[/img]
The Demo [b]includes 4 achievements[/b], 3 of them being hidden (because they are related to the story), and the only visible one being the [i]Golden Carpinchos[/i], small collectibles that can be find them distributed throughout the level, [i]If you find them all you will obtain the achievement![/i]
Remember that the Demo does not represent the final product, and it is very likely that several things will tend to be different or change completely.

[h2]Memories of past... and future events[/h2]
The Demo that is public on Steam right now is the updated version of the one we originally published on Itch.io. One of the most notable differences is that this Demo had a time limit, something that was removed for later versions, and that will only be used in versions for events.

On May 5th, this demo was presented live at the [i]"Star Wars Rosario Fan Club Celebration"[/i] (Rosario, Santa Fe, Argentina), a charity event that, despite being Star Wars-themed, we were given the opportunity to show the demo of the game in our humble Stand to hundreds or even thousands of people. People of all ages had the chance to play the demo at the booth, with a really positive reception!
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/9b2beeb31ac88866fbe4de2a80c4419164b89efd.jpg[/img]
We want to wholeheartedly thank the people of [i]Star Wars Rosario Fan Club Celebration[/i] and the party hall [i]"La Opera”[/i] for giving us this incredible opportunity, it was an unforgettable experience !
Thanks to people's feedback, we thought about improvements for the game and the Demo and the stand itself, with the possibility of being present at other conventions or local events... Like the well-known [b]"Crack Bang Boom"[/ b] from Rosario!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/5ad0a7b3357f4292ff731fb63ec5f42d868f6642.png[/img]
[h3]Those who are from Rosario, know that we will be present at the event with our Stand from Thursday the 15th to Sunday the 18th, with the possibility of playing the Demo live, chatting with the Devs and even who knows... getting exclusive merchandising! [/h3]

[h2]Improved Systems - Player Movement and Inventory[/h2]
In recent weeks, one of our programmers, [i]Alejandro[/i], has been working on a complete overhaul of the Player movement system and the Inventory system. These were written from scratch, implementing various Unity systems that will allow us in the future to improve player inputs, Control compatibility (Xbox Controllers, Playstation, etc.) and even improvements to the game's cinematics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/45f6a3a2b7e1b58266fc3e613822f36e0c06a77e.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/1fede2c115a0b597eeb14c5904867f0b18895753.gif[/img]

[i](Keep in mind that everything shown is still in development and is subject to change, almost all visual elements shown as models or animations are Placeholders and are not representative of the final product)[/i]

The player can now crouch and see his own body when looking down. In addition, the animations of the player's "camera" or "POV" were improved, which will now never be fixed and will have different animations depending on the player's movements, giving greater realism and immersion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/7433081d248612957f0f778d26a8a400b3fcaf51.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/7e71edf64c24c9b509594b27237fb72938b755e3.gif[/img]

In the case of the Inventory, the vast majority of functionalities are already finished, with some touches missing such as the visuals

[b]All these changes are not reflected in the current Demo, but will be present directly in the final version of the game.[/b]

[h2]Steps towards the future[/h2]
In the following months, we will be 100% focused on improving some remaining aspects of the first level, in order to move on to the full development of the other following levels, especially [b]The Parking[/b] and [b]The Mansion[/b]. 

At the same time, we will do everything possible to make ourselves seen even more, through devblogs, teasers and posts on social networks, participating in multiple events such as the aforementioned [i]Crack Bang Boom[/i] and the [i]Steam Next October Fest[/i] (which we are already registered for!), and with a little luck, events like the [i]EVA PLAY[/i] or the [i]Future Games Show[/i] August.

[h2]That's all![/h2]
We hope you have enjoyed this first Devblog here on Steam, and that you stay tuned for the coming months, as very interesting and important things are coming for the project.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45063930/5317c08a2f69b9f1f0321f603895ac9cff45d9e3.jpg[/img]
See you in the next Devblog!
